text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the appointee are women, so an all-female panel points nowhere useful. Panel composition on its own isn't evidence of anything — it's common in many departments and says nothing about how they weighed candidates. Raising it would read as a grievance in search of a theory and would undercut your credibility on the point that actually has force.

Your real complaint is strong without it: a public body appointed a candidate with a weaker formal record on paper and has ignored a written request for reasons for two weeks. In most jurisdictions you have a right to reasons and to see the scoring criteria. Send a dated follow-up, copy HR, and ask for the assessment documentation.
